rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act (HSNA) – Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources
rules.requirement: A landlord or foreclosing owner ending a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources at the same time as the Notice to Quit or notice of lease non-renewal. The landlord must also send a copy of the Notice to Quit or Notice of Non-renewal, with a Certificate of Compliance/Service, to the City of Boston’s Office of Housing Stability.
rules.coverage_text: All landlords and foreclosing owners intending to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a unit in the City of Boston, including when starting the eviction process or when deciding not to offer a lease renewal.
rules.exemptions: Residences in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility; and residences in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is providing short-term treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug, or other substance abuse.
rules.penalty: 1st offense: warning; 2nd and subsequent offenses: $300 per day, enforced by the Inspectional Services Department. A violation does not halt the eviction process.
rules.quoted_span: The HSNA requires that landlords give this Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources to tenants when the landlord starts the eviction process, or when the landlord decides to not offer the tenant a renewal of their lease agreement.
rules.effective_date_phrase: The HSNA becomes effective on November 6, 2020.
